$comment: THE central registry of accounts the bench uses. Specs resolve accounts by ROLE through
src/fixtures/test-accounts.ts and never hard-code a KPost ID.
The first six accounts are PRE-EXISTING ones declared in .env, not created by the bench.
The qatestN accounts (no underscore: the product rejects one in a KPost ID) are created by
scripts/provision-test-accounts.cjs; each is marked provisioned here only after it logs in.
NO IDs OR PASSWORDS LIVE IN THIS FILE. Both are POINTERS to environment variables
(kpostIdEnv / passwordEnv). The file is committed; .env is not.

rationale: Verified against KPOST_QA (active accounts): PERSONAL @kpostindia.com 324, PERSONAL
An account marked legacyDomain: true is a personal account on the business domain. It is
pre-existing data, NOT a defect and NOT something to rewrite — kpost_id is the primary key
across ~90 tables. The flag exists so the mismatch is declared rather than silently tolerated.
blockedByProduct: Signup REJECTS any kpostID whose local part contains an UNDERSCORE, answering HTTP 200 with
{statusCode: 500, message: "Enter valid Credentials"}. Decisive test: two otherwise identical
payloads with distinct mobiles — qatest_sender@kpostindia.com refused, qatestsender@kpostindia.com
not refused for that reason. Corroborated: 0 of 2,167 accounts on KPOST_QA contain an underscore.

accounts.purpose: The bench's own account: sender in 1:1 flows and caller for profile reads. On the legacy @kpost.in domain.
The receiver in 1:1 Katchup and KMail flows, and the second session for isolation probes.
A third party: Cc, confidential-copy invisibility (NFR-SEC02) and a group of three.
Administrator of the BUSINESS_M company (Nebius, 242); drives the Admin permission workflows.
An ordinary member of that company: the subject of permission and role checks.
The third member, so a company of three can be exercised. NEVER terminated — the Admin DB is live-adjacent and members cannot be recreated via API.
Record owner in ownership (BOLA) checks: creates the message, call, group or document that a stranger must not reach.
The stranger in ownership checks: a different user who must be refused the owner's records.
Third party in group, Cc / confidential-copy and multi-recipient flows.
Fourth party: second group member and second recipient.
Sacrificial target: the account the destructive sweep blocks, deletes, calls and adds, so nothing shared is touched.
Spare: account-lockout and limited forgot-password probes (the forgot-password OTP is real on the live host, so keep it to a few calls).
